evidence.curator_note: Step 3 of Equation 8.21 (the reaction arrow is labelled 'alpha'). Text: after the gamma-H/beta-cleavage (record IMS8-EQ8.21a) 'the molecule of N-methylacetamide enol remains in the vicinity of the ion and moves across the steroid skeleton to form a stabilized hydrogen-bond complex with the 20-amino group. This eventually dissociates by alpha-cleavage to form the ion at m/z 103.' The precursor here is the ion-neutral complex of the steroid-ene aminium radical cation (n-ionized 20-amine, -CH2-NH2+.) hydrogen-bonded to the neutral enol (drawn bottom-right as -CH2-NH....H+....N=C(OH)CH3). alpha-cleavage breaks the C17-C20 bond (map25-map26) beta to the aminium nitrogen and forms the C20=N iminium double bond (map26=map27), expelling the neutral steroid radical (radical at C17, map25) and giving the methyleniminium ion CH2=NH2+ (m/z 30). ARC COUNT (convention D): the book draws 2 arcs at the -CH2-NH group, both single-barbed fishhooks that FORM the new C=N pi bond -- one from the aminium N odd electron (encoded move 1: atom(27)->bond(26,27)) and one from a C17-C20 bonding electron (encoded move 2: bond(25,26)->bond(26,27)). Book draws 2 arc(s); moves <1,2> are drawn, move <3> (the second C17-C20 bonding electron onto the departing steroid radical C17, bond(25,26)->atom(25)) is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page -- the neutral steroid radical is not drawn as a separate product at all). NON-COVALENT COMPLEX (convention G): the observed ion m/z 103 is drawn as a proton-bound complex, HO-C(CH3)=N(CH3)....H+....HN=CH2, i.e. the N-methylacetamide enol (73.0528) hydrogen-bonded through a shared proton to methanimine; it is NOT a single covalent species, so it is encoded here as its net components -- the methyleniminium cation (map26,27; 30.0333) plus the neutral enol spectator (73.0528), whose masses sum to the m/z 103.0860 (nominal 103) printed under the structure. The extra bridging proton is the aminium's own N-H engaged in the H-bond to the enol nitrogen; no separate proton transfer is needed for the covalent alpha-cleavage. CHARGE/RADICAL (convention B): charge and odd electron localized on the 20-amino nitrogen per the aminium radical cation (see record a). SUBSTRATE (convention F): same curator-chosen 20-aminomethyl-androstene realization as record a; the steroid backbone is a spectator to the alpha-cleavage.

evidence.curator_note: DRAWN INTERMEDIATE STEP NOT ENCODED AS AN ELEMENTARY STEP (disclosure per convention G). Between record a and this record the page draws a second arrow (the vertical arrow that carries the equation number 8.21): the neutral N-methylacetamide enol 'moves across the steroid skeleton' (indicated by a long dashed curved arrow sweeping from the enol nitrogen up to the 20-amino group) and forms a 'stabilized hydrogen-bond complex' with the 20-amino group (drawn as -CH2-NH....H+....N=C(OH)CH3 with two dotted H-bond lines and the '+' on the bridging H). This migration/complexation changes NO covalent bonds -- it is a conformational / ion-dipole rearrangement of the ion-neutral complex -- so it has zero electron-pushing arcs and cannot be represented as an ElementaryStep (the schema requires >=1 electron_move). It is therefore folded into the boundary between records a and b: the covalent species entering this alpha-cleavage (state_complex) is identical to the species leaving record a, merely reorganized in space so the enol nitrogen sits next to the 20-amino group. The text stresses this remote-group approach is the low-energy path ('other pathways...would require much more energy, either to bend the rigid steroid skeleton or to cleave several C-C' bonds).

NO MØD rule is cross-linked: rule_index.json by_equation has no '8.21' key, so there is no Rule.fromDFS encoding for this equation and nothing to verify against. rule_mismatches: none (nothing to compare against).

The book prints 'm/z 103' under the bottom-left structure (a nominal, printed mass) but no relative intensity, so relative_intensity is omitted (convention F). observed_mz 103.0860 is the curator-computed monoisotopic m/z of the drawn proton-bound complex C4H11N2O+ = methyleniminium CH2=NH2+ (30.0333) + N-methylacetamide enol (73.0528). The peak is attached to the methyleniminium ion because that is the charge-carrying covalent species; the true detected ion is the enol...H+...HN=CH2 proton-bound complex (see step evidence, convention G).
